The story uses sophisticated metaphor to connect Ruth’s desire for certainty with the baby’s physical weight: “seven pounds two ounces of certainty” transforms bodily substance into emotional reassurance and moral denial. Describing anesthesia as “a long, featureless country with no roads” conveys both disorientation and lost agency. The idiom “clean as a whistle” also gains disturbing significance when its repetition turns routine reassurance into evidence of the baby’s switched identity.
